title: Bounded async pipeline
prompt:
Implement `async def pipeline(items, transform, workers=2, maxsize=3)`:

- put all `items` through an `asyncio.Queue(maxsize=maxsize)`
- `workers` async tasks consume and append `await transform(item)` results
- the producer must NOT dump everything into the queue at once — with maxsize honored, queue backpressure applies (`await q.put` suspends when full)
- return `sorted(results)` after `await q.join()`; cancel the workers afterwards
boilerplate:
import asyncio

# TODO: pipeline(items, transform, workers=2, maxsize=3)

tests.name: processes all items with backpressure safe
tests.code:
async def dbl(x):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
    return x * 2

loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
out = loop.run_until_complete(pipeline([3, 1, 2, 5, 4], dbl, workers=2, maxsize=2))
loop.close()
assert out == [2, 4, 6, 8, 10], f'out: {out}'
print('ok')
tests.hint: q.join() releases only when every queued item has task_done() called; put() suspends when the bounded queue is full.

tests.name: many items through a tiny queue
tests.code:
async def ident(x):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
    return x

loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
out = loop.run_until_complete(pipeline(list(range(60)), ident, workers=3, maxsize=2))
loop.close()
assert out == list(range(60))
print('ok')
tests.hint: 60 items must flow through a maxsize-2 queue without deadlock.
